subject: math

entries: Arithmetic progressions: add d each step: starting from 5 with d = 3, the marker hops the axis in equal jumps through 5, 8, 11, 14, and u_n = a + (n - 1)d counts the n - 1 jumps made before term n.
slots.label: Arithmetic progressions
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Geometric progressions: multiply by r each step: with r = 2 the terms 2, 4, 8, 16 double each time, the jumps widen, and u_n = a x r^(n - 1) applies r once per jump.
slots.label: Geometric progressions
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Seeing the sum build up: each new term drops into the running total - 2, then 6, then 12, then 20 for 2, 4, 6, 8 - and pairing first with last turns the buildup into S_n = (n/2)(a + l).
slots.label: Seeing the sum build up
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: A common mistake: r = -1 never settles: the terms bounce 1, -1, 1, -1 forever, and only a shrinking ratio with |r| < 1 lets the terms home in on a limit and the sum settle at a / (1 - r).
slots.label: A common mistake
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: The sequences toolkit: the a and d chips drop into u_n = a + (n - 1)d, then a and r into u_n = a x r^(n - 1) - two formulas, four moving parts, and in both the count is jumps, not terms.
slots.label: The sequences toolkit
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: A sequence that adds the same common difference d at every step: starting from 5 with d = 3, the terms are 5, 8, 11, 14, and the marker hops the axis in equal jumps.
slots.label: Arithmetic progression
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A sequence that multiplies by the same common ratio r at every step: with r = 2, the terms 2, 4, 8, 16 double each time and the jumps widen.
slots.label: Geometric progression
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The fixed amount d added between consecutive terms of an arithmetic progression: d = u_2 - u_1, so d = 3 for 5, 8, 11, 14.
slots.label: Common difference
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The fixed factor r multiplied between consecutive terms of a geometric progression: r = u_2 / u_1, so r = 2 for 2, 4, 8, 16.
slots.label: Common ratio
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The general term u_n of a sequence: u_n = a + (n - 1)d for an arithmetic progression and u_n = a x r^(n - 1) for a geometric one, where n - 1 counts the jumps from the first term.
slots.label: nth term
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The sum S_n of the first n terms, built up one term at a time: for 2, 4, 6, 8, the partial sums run S_1 = 2, S_2 = 6, S_3 = 12, S_4 = 20, and for an arithmetic progression S_n = (n/2)(a + l).
slots.label: Partial sum
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

title: JC H2 sequences: arithmetic and geometric progressions
